correctness.rationale: Over the exact domain k>=2, odd first-coordinate sums give invertible 3s and two simple roots; even first-coordinate sums reduce uniquely to square roots modulo 2^(k-1), including all zero and low-valuation cases. The histogram and image size follow from the 2-adic unit-square counts; the independent zero-product count gives E=kN^2. Newton recurrence proves that three moments determine all higher ones, and an explicit pair proves two insufficient. Fourier orthogonality gives the normalized fourth moment. Extracted exact checker enumerates all positive fibers and energy/image through k=10, but finite tests do not prove the all-k statement.

value.rationale: The canonical 3-dimensional cubic moment curve is the first natural moment embedding for which Newton inversion has a 2-adic obstruction. A sharp minimum moment threshold, exact all-target two-point convolution, valuation-dependent histogram, 7/24 asymptotic image density and logarithmically growing normalized energy describe a genuine structural boundary for finite-ring restriction. The object is natural and the exact invariant is useful independent of a broader sharp weighted inequality.
